answer:
Let the west wall be \(x=0\), the east wall \(x=14\), the south side \(y=0\), and the north side \(y=9\).

Assume the gate 3 m from the west wall is on the north side and the gate 10 m from the west wall is on the south side:

\[
G_1=(3,9),\qquad G_2=(10,0).
\]

To minimize the path from \(G_1\) to \(G_2\) touching the west wall, reflect \(G_2\) across \(x=0\):

\[
G_2'=(-10,0).
\]

The shortest broken path becomes the straight segment \(G_1G_2'\). Its intersection with the west wall \(x=0\) is the contact point \(P\).

Parametrize the line from \(G_1=(3,9)\) to \(G_2'=(-10,0)\):

\[
(x,y)=(3,9)+t(-13,-9).
\]

Set \(x=0\):

\[
3-13t=0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad t=\frac{3}{13}.
\]

Then

\[
y=9-9t=9-\frac{27}{13}
=\frac{90}{13}.
\]

Thus the contact point is

\[
P=\left(0,\frac{90}{13}\right)
\approx (0,6.923).
\]

Since

\[
0<\frac{90}{13}<9,
\]

the point lies on the west wall segment.

The shortest route length is the straight distance from \(G_1\) to \(G_2'\):

\[
\sqrt{(3+10)^2+(9-0)^2}
=\sqrt{13^2+9^2}
=\sqrt{250}
=5\sqrt{10}\ \text{m}
\approx 15.81\ \text{m}.
\]

So the shortest route goes from one gate to the west wall at a height of \(\frac{90}{13}\) m above the south wall, then to the other gate.

If the 3 m and 10 m gates are on the opposite long sides instead, the contact point is the mirror-height

\[
P=\left(0,\frac{27}{13}\right),
\]

and the total shortest length is still \(5\sqrt{10}\) m.
